Rashi on Ketubot 36a:10:1.hebrew: נותנין לה לילה הראשון - ובועל כמה בעילות, ותלינן כל דמים של אותו הלילה בדם בתולים. אלמא, אית לה דם בתולים לבוגרת, דאי לא, לא הוה בעי למיתב לה אלא בעילת מצוה. וכיון דאית לה בתולים, היכא דבעל ולא מצא דם, תפסיד כתובתה, דהא כנסה בחזקת בתולה ומצאה בעולה:
Rashi on Ketubot 36a:10:1.english: [The Sages] give her the first night - And he may engage in intercourse several times, and we attribute all blood of that night to hymenal blood. Thus, a grown woman [bogeret] has hymenal blood, for if not, it would not be necessary to give her [permission for] anything other than the intercourse of the mitzvah. And since she has [signs of] virginity, where he engaged in intercourse and did not find blood, she should forfeit her ketubah, for he married her on the presumption that she was a virgin and found her to be a non-virgin.

Rashi on Ketubot 36a:1:1.hebrew: עריות ממש - המפורש באחרי מות, והן בכריתות:
Rashi on Ketubot 36a:1:1.english: Actual forbidden relatives - [That which is] explicitly stated in [the portion of] Acharei Mot, and they are [punishable by] karet.

Rashi on Ketubot 36a:1:2.hebrew: שניות - שגזרו חכמים על שניות להן להרחיק מן העבירה, כגון אם אמו ואם אביו ושאר עריות השנויות בפרק ב' דיבמות (דף כא.):
Rashi on Ketubot 36a:1:2.english: Secondary [relatives] - [meaning] that the Sages decreed regarding [relatives] secondary to them to distance [a person] from transgression, such as his mother's mother and his father's mother, and the rest of the forbidden relatives taught in the second chapter of Yevamot (21a).

Rashi on Ketubot 36a:1:3.english: Since secondary [relatives] are suitable for him by Torah law - we read regarding it, "and she shall be to him as a wife."

Rashi on Ketubot 36a:1:4.hebrew: אמאי אין לה קנס - בשלמא בעריות איכא למימר כשמעון התימני, דלית ליה "נערה נערה הנערה", אלא שניות קשיא:
Rashi on Ketubot 36a:1:4.english: Why does she not have a fine - Granted, regarding forbidden relatives, one can say [it accords] with Shimon HaTimni, who does not hold of [the exposition of] "a maiden, a maiden, the maiden," but [regarding] secondary relatives, it is difficult.

Rashi on Ketubot 36a:1:5.english: Shimon HaTimni - At the beginning of our chapter, where he said [that the fine applies to] a woman with whom betrothal is effective.

Rashi on Ketubot 36a:2:1.hebrew: ר"ש בן מנסיא - דאמר אשה הראויה לקיימה:
Rashi on Ketubot 36a:2:1.english: Rabbi Shimon ben Menasya - Who says: "a woman fit to be kept [in marriage]."

Rashi on Ketubot 36a:3:1.hebrew: רבנן היא - דפליגי אדר"מ בריש פירקין:
Rashi on Ketubot 36a:3:1.english: It is [the opinion of] the Rabbis - who disagree with Rabbi Meir at the beginning of our chapter.

Rashi on Ketubot 36a:4:1.hebrew: ובממאנת סבר לה כר' יהודה - דאמר נערה ממאנת, והכי תידוק מינה: נערה ממאנת אין לה קנס, הא נערה בעלמא יש לה קנס:
Rashi on Ketubot 36a:4:1.english: And with regard to [a girl] who refuses, he holds in accordance with Rabbi Yehuda - Who says [that] a young woman can refuse, and thus you would infer from it: a young woman who refuses has no fine, whereas an ordinary young woman does have a fine.

Rashi on Ketubot 36a:4:2.hebrew: עד שתביא שתי שערות - ומשהביאה אינה ממאנת, ואפילו לא בעל לאחר מיכן:
Rashi on Ketubot 36a:4:2.english: Until she develops two [pubic] hairs - And once she has developed [them], she cannot refuse, even if he did not have marital relations [with her] afterward.

Rashi on Ketubot 36a:4:3.hebrew: רבי יהודה אומר - אם לא בעל לאחר שגדלה, ממאנת:
Rashi on Ketubot 36a:4:3.english: Rabbi Yehuda says - If [he] did not have marital relations [with her] after she grew up, she may refuse [the marriage].

Rashi on Ketubot 36a:4:4.hebrew: עד שירבה שחור על הלבן - ובנדה מפרש: שתי שערות שוכבות, ונראה כמו שירבה השחור:
Rashi on Ketubot 36a:4:4.english: Until the black exceeds the white - And in [Tractate] Niddah it explains: [this means] two hairs lying flat, so that it appears as though the black exceeds [the white].

Rashi on Ketubot 36a:5:1.hebrew: אלא ר' יהודה היא - ובממאנת נערה אשמעינן דאין לה קנס, ולא תדוק "הא קטנה יש לה קנס". וגבי אילונית דתנא נמי אין לה קנס, משום דבקטנה סבר כר"מ, וזו מקטנותה יצאת לבגר:
Rashi on Ketubot 36a:5:1.english: Rather, it is [the opinion of] Rabbi Yehuda - And regarding a girl who exercises the right of refusal, it teaches us [about] a na'arah [young woman] that she has no fine, and do not infer [from this]: "Thus, a minor has a fine." And regarding an ailonit, where it also taught [that] she has no fine, [that is] because with regard to a minor he holds like Rabbi Meir, and this [woman] went [directly] from her minority to adulthood.

Rashi on Ketubot 36a:5:2.english: This is the statement, etc. - Below in our chapter (Ketubot 40b).

Rashi on Ketubot 36a:5:3.hebrew: סבר לה כר' מאיר - דקטנה אין לה קנס, משום הכי אין קנס באילונית:
Rashi on Ketubot 36a:5:3.english: He holds in accordance with Rabbi Meir - That a minor [girl] has no fine; therefore, there is no fine for an ailonit.

Rashi on Ketubot 36a:5:4.hebrew: ופליג עליה - בממאנת, ואמר עד שירבה השחור. וכי תנא הממאנת אין לה קנס, הא הראויה למאן יש לה קנס — בנערה קאמר:
Rashi on Ketubot 36a:5:4.english: And disagrees with him - Regarding [a girl who] exercises refusal, and [he] says [she may refuse] until the black [pubic hair] predominates. And when [the baraita] taught: "One who exercises refusal has no fine," [implying that] one who is eligible to refuse has a fine — it is speaking of a na'arah.

Rashi on Ketubot 36a:6:1.hebrew: מאי ממאנת הראויה למאן - כלומר, כל קטנה קאמר, וכולה ר"מ היא:
Rashi on Ketubot 36a:6:1.english: What is "one who refuses"? One who is fit to refuse - That is to say, he means any minor, and the entire [baraita] is [in accordance with] Rabbi Meir.

Rashi on Ketubot 36a:7:1.english: And they have a claim of virginity - To cause her to lose [her] marriage contract.

Rashi on Ketubot 36a:7:2.hebrew: הא ר"מ - דאמר קטנה אין לה קנס, ואילונית מקטנותה יצתה לבגר:
Rashi on Ketubot 36a:7:2.english: This [is] Rabbi Meir - Who says [that] a minor has no fine, and an ailonit passes from her minority [directly] to adulthood.

Rashi on Ketubot 36a:7:3.hebrew: ודקארי לה מאי קארי לה - מי שהשיב תשובה זו בבית המדרש, מה עלתה על רוחו, ולא סבירא ליה דאיכא לאוקמינהו כר"מ ורבנן:
Rashi on Ketubot 36a:7:3.english: And he who raised it, why did he raise it - He who raised this objection in the study hall — what entered his mind, that he did not think it possible to establish them in accordance with Rabbi Meir and the Rabbis?

Rashi on Ketubot 36a:8:1.hebrew: משום דאית ליה למירמא אחריתא עליה - לא הביאה לבית המדרש אלא לפי שיש להשיב אחרת על זו, חרשת ושוטה אחרשת ושוטה:
Rashi on Ketubot 36a:8:1.english: Because he has another [baraita] to cast against it - He only brought it to the study hall because there is another [baraita] to raise in objection against this one — [the case of] a deaf-mute and an imbecile against [the case of] a deaf-mute and an imbecile.

Rashi on Ketubot 36a:8:2.english: A grown woman - Her virginity wears away on its own.

Rashi on Ketubot 36a:9:1.hebrew: הא רבן גמליאל - דאמר בפ"ק (דף יב:): "היא אומרת משאירסתני נאנסתי, נאמנת". הכא נמי, אין לה טענת בתולים להפסידה כתובתה, דאמרינן: אי הוה פקחת לטעון, הוה טענה "משאירסתני נאנסתי" ומהימנא:
Rashi on Ketubot 36a:9:1.english: This [is] Rabban Gamliel - Who said in the first chapter (12b): "[If] she says, 'After you betrothed me, I was raped,' she is believed." Here too, there is no claim of [non-]virginity [against] her to make her forfeit her marriage contract, for we say [that] if she were competent to plead, she would plead, "After you betrothed me, I was raped," and she would be believed.

Rashi on Ketubot 36a:9:2.hebrew: הא רבי יהושע - דאמר לא מפיה אנו חיין, הכא יש לה טענת בתולים, דאי נמי הוה טענה קמן, לא מהימנינן לה:
Rashi on Ketubot 36a:9:2.english: This [is] Rabbi Yehoshua - Who says, "We do not live by her mouth" [i.e., we do not rely on her word]; here, there is a virginity claim [against her], for even if she were to make a claim before us, we would not believe her.

Tosafot on Ketubot 36a:1:1.hebrew: [אבל חייבי לאוין יש להן קנס ומני שמעון התימני היא - לא הוה מצי למימר "מני רבי נחוניא היא", דלדידיה לא הוה קרי להו "שניות", שהרי משוה חייבי כריתות לחייבי מיתות ב"ד. והא דלא קאמר "הא מני? רבי עקיבא, ועריות חייבי מיתות, ושניות חייבי כריתות וחייבי לאוין" — אלא דניחא ליה לאוקמי אפי' כרבנן דאמרי קידושין תופסין; ועוד, משום דקאמר בלישנא קמא "מני שמעון התימני היא", קאמר נמי באיכא דאמרי "מני רבי שמעון בן מנסיא היא", דהוי בר פלוגתיה דשמעון התימני]:
Tosafot on Ketubot 36a:1:1.english: "However, those liable for regular prohibitions receive a fine, and whose [opinion] is it? It is [the opinion of] Shimon HaTimni." - [The Gemara] could not say, "Whose [opinion] is it? It is [that of] Rabbi Nechunya [ben HaKanah]," for according to him it would not call them "secondary [relatives]," since he equates those liable to karet with those liable to a court-imposed death penalty. And [the reason] it does not say, "Whose [opinion] is this? Rabbi Akiva['s], and 'forbidden relatives' [means] those liable to death, and 'secondary [relatives]' [means] those liable to karet and those liable for regular prohibitions" — [is] rather because it prefers to establish [the baraita] even according to the Rabbis, who say [that] betrothal takes effect [with those liable for regular prohibitions]. And furthermore, because it says in the first version, "Whose [opinion] is it? It is Shimon HaTimni['s]," it also says in the "there are those who say" [version], "Whose [opinion] is it? It is Rabbi Shimon ben Menasya['s]," who is the disputant of Shimon HaTimni.

Tosafot on Ketubot 36a:4:1.hebrew: עד שירבה השחור כו' - אית דלא גרסי "על הלבן", משום דאמרינן בפרק בא סימן (נדה דף נב. ושם): לא שירבה ממש, אלא כדי שיהו שתי שערות שוכבות ונראה כמו שירבה שחור; ו"על הלבן" משמע יותר מן הלבן. ור"ח פירש: "על הלבן" — שהשערות סמוך לבשר הם שחורים, ובראשם לבנים:
Tosafot on Ketubot 36a:4:1.english: "Until the black is greater, etc." - There are those who do not read [the words] "than the white" [in the baraita], because we say in Chapter Ba Siman (Niddah 52a and [also] there): [This does] not [mean] that it literally becomes greater, but rather enough so that two hairs lie flat and it appears as though the black is abundant; whereas "than the white" implies [that the black is actually] more than the white. And Rabbeinu Chananel explained "on the white" [to mean] that the hairs near the flesh are black, and at their tips they are white.

Tosafot on Ketubot 36a:5:1.hebrew: זו דברי ר"מ - אמתניתין דלקמן (כתובות דף מ:), דכל מקום שיש מכר אין קנס, קאמר לה רב יהודה:
Tosafot on Ketubot 36a:5:1.english: "This is the statement of Rabbi Meir" - Rav Yehuda says this regarding the Mishnah below (Ketubot 40b), [which states] that wherever there is [the right of] sale, there is no fine.

Tosafot on Ketubot 36a:5:2.hebrew: ואם איתא, זו דברי ר"מ ורבי יהודה מיבעי ליה - ואע"ג דרבי יונתן ור' יאשיה סבירא להו כר"מ בס"פ ד' מיתות (סנהדרין סו: ושם) — לפי' ר"ת, דפי' "עד שיהיו שניהם שוין במיתה אחת", ואפי' לפ"ה, דמפרש "בני עונשין", מ"מ ר' יאשיה כר' מאיר סבירא ליה, דלית ליה הא דדרשי רבנן לקמן (כתובות דף מ:) "כאן נערה" כו', דהא פטר קטנה מאורסה — מ"מ לא קאמר "זו דברי ר"מ ור' יאשיה"; דלא פריך הכא "זו דברי ר"מ ורבי יהודה מיבעי ליה", אלא משום דרבי יהודה בר פלוגתיה דר"מ, והוי בכלל חכמים דפליגי עליה; ולהכי, אם איתא דלא פליג, ה"ל למימר "זו דברי ר"מ ור' יהודה". אבל קשה, דה"ל למימר: הא מני? ר' יאשיה היא, ובממאנת סבר לה כר' יהודה:
Tosafot on Ketubot 36a:5:2.english: And if it is so, he should have said: "This is the statement of Rabbi Meir and Rabbi Yehuda" - Even though Rabbi Yonatan and Rabbi Yoshiyah hold in accordance with Rabbi Meir at the end of the chapter [entitled] Arba Mitot (Sanhedrin 66b and elsewhere) — according to the explanation of Rabbeinu Tam, who explained [the phrase there as]: "until both of them are equal in one [and the same] death penalty," and even according to Rashi's explanation, who explains [it as]: "subject to punishments," nevertheless Rabbi Yoshiyah holds in accordance with Rabbi Meir, for he does not hold of that which the Rabbis expound below (Ketubot 40b): "Here [it states] 'a young woman' (na'arah), etc.," since he indeed exempts a betrothed minor girl — nevertheless, [Rav] did not say: "This is the statement of Rabbi Meir and Rabbi Yoshiyah"; for [the Gemara] only asks here "he should have said: This is the statement of Rabbi Meir and Rabbi Yehuda" because Rabbi Yehuda is Rabbi Meir's disputant and is included among the Sages who disagree with him; and therefore, if it were so that he does not disagree [with him on this], [Rav] should have said: "This is the statement of Rabbi Meir and Rabbi Yehuda." However, it is difficult: [why didn't the Gemara] say, "Whose [opinion] is this? It is Rabbi Yoshiyah, and with regard to a girl who refuses [her marriage], he holds in accordance with Rabbi Yehuda"?

Tosafot on Ketubot 36a:6:1.hebrew: וליתני קטנה קשיא - אע"ג דהוי תני קטנה דאין לה קנס, מ"מ תני נמי אילונית, דה"א דוקא קטנה שיש לה נערות אין לה קנס. ותימה לר"י: אמאי לא משני דאגב אורחיה קמ"ל דעד מתי הבת ממאנת — עד שתביא שתי שערות:
Tosafot on Ketubot 36a:6:1.english: And let [the tanna] teach "a minor"; [this is] difficult - Even though it would have taught [that] a minor has no fine, nevertheless it also teaches [the case of] an ailonit, for one might have thought [that] specifically a minor, who has [a stage of] na'arut, has no fine. And it is astonishing to the Ri: why does [the Gemara] not answer that incidentally it teaches us until when a daughter may refuse — until she brings two [pubic] hairs?

Tosafot on Ketubot 36a:8:1.hebrew: החרשת והשוטה כו' אין להן טענת בתולים - פי' בקונטרס: דאי הוה פקחת לטעון, הוה טענה "משאירסתני נאנסתי". וקשה לר"י: דהיכי טענינן לה הכי מספק לאפוקי ממונא, כיון דאיהי לא טענה? דחזקת גופה איתרעי, דהוי שור שחוט לפניך, אבל חזקת ממון לא איתרע! ומיהו מביא ר"י ראיה לפי' הקונטרס, דאמר בפ' המדיר (לקמן כתובות עו: ושם): "לא הוגלד פי המכה, המוציא מחבירו עליו הראיה", ומפרש דאפי' לא יהיב טבח דמי, על הטבח להביא ראיה שברשות המוכר נטרפה. והא דמפרש רב אשי למתני' דהמדיר ד"היו בה מומין ועודה בבית אביה, על האב להביא ראיה" — רישא "מנה לאבא בידך", סיפא "מנה לי בידך" — לא מטעם דברי ושמא ברי עדיף, כדמשמע לפום ריהטא, דא"כ הוה קשה: דהיכי טענינן לה הכי? אלא כדפי' התם בקונטרס: רישא "מנה לאבא בידך" — דלגבי האב לא מהני חזקת הגוף דבתו, דהכתובה היא באירוסין של אב; סיפא "מנה לי בידך" — דלגבי דידה מהני חזקת הגוף דידה. וכן צריך לפרש, דאי מטעם ברי קאמר התם, אמאי קאמר ד"עודה בבית אביה, על האב להביא ראיה דמשנתארסה נולדו בה מומין"? אמאי צריך להביא ראיה כיון דאמר "ברי לי"? דבכל ענין משמע דצריך להביא ראיה, אפילו אב אמר "ברי לי"! ולר"י נראה לפרש הכא: דאין להן טענת בתולים לפי שבחזקת מוכת עץ היא. ואע"ג דכולהו נמי חבוטי מחבטן, מ"מ שאר נשים יש להן טענת בתולים מדלא קאמרי שהן מוכת עץ; אבל הנך — חרשת ושוטה — דלא מצי אמרי, בחזקת מוכת עץ נשאות. וכן נראה, דברוב ספרים ל"ג לעיל בברייתא אלא "החרשת והשוטה והאילונית יש להן קנס" ותו לא, ואין כתוב ברוב ספרים "ויש להן טענת בתולים". ולפר"י פריך שפיר, דמדקאמר "יש להן קנס", אלמא לא חשבינן להו בחזקת מוכת עץ; אבל לפי' הקונטרס מאי קפריך? הכא נמי בחזקת בתולות חשבינן להו, דהא אמרינן השתא דמשנתארסה נאנסה! ורשב"א הקשה לפר"י: דאמאי לא משני הא דקתני "אין להן טענת בתולים" כר"מ, דאמר בפ"ק (לעיל כתובות יג.): "מוכת עץ, בין הכיר בה בין לא הכיר בה — מאתים", והא דקתני "יש להן טענת בתולים" כרבנן דאמרי כתובתן מנה? וכי תימא משום דקתני חרשת דומיא דאיילונית — הא ע"כ איילונית גופה לא הפסידה כתובתה לגמרי, דהא רב ששת דמשני "הא ר"ג, הא ר' יהושע" סבירא ליה בפ"ק (דף יא:): כנסה בחזקת בתולה ונמצאת בעולה — יש לה כתובה מנה:
Tosafot on Ketubot 36a:8:1.english: "A deaf-mute, and an imbecile, etc., do not have a claim concerning virginity" - Rashi explained that if she were of sound mind to make a claim, she would claim, "After you betrothed me, I was violated." And it is difficult for R"I: how could we make such a claim on her behalf out of doubt to extract money [from the husband], since she herself does not claim [it]? For the presumptive status of her body has been weakened, as it is [a case of] "a slaughtered ox before you," whereas the presumptive status of the money [remaining with the husband] has not been weakened! Nevertheless, R"I brings a proof for Rashi's explanation, for [the Gemara] says in chapter HaMadir (below, Ketubot 76b, and there): "[If] the mouth of the wound has not scabbed over, the burden of proof is upon the one who seeks to extract [money] from his fellow," and [the Gemara] explains that even if the butcher has not [yet] paid the money, it is upon the butcher to bring proof that it became tereifah while in the seller's possession. And that which Rav Ashi explains the Mishnah of HaMadir — [regarding] where she had blemishes while still in her father's house, it is upon the father to bring proof — [that] the first clause [is a case of] "my father has a maneh in your hand" [and] the second clause [is a case of] "I have a maneh in your hand," is not for the reason that [between] a certain [claim] and an uncertain [claim], the certain [claim] is stronger, as appears at first glance — for if so, it would be difficult: how do we make such a claim on her behalf [here]? — rather, [it is] as Rashi explained there: [in] the first clause, "my father has a maneh in your hand," with respect to the father, the presumptive status of his daughter's body is not effective, since the ketubah [belongs to the father] during the betrothal [arranged] by the father; [in] the second clause, "I have a maneh in your hand," with respect to her, the presumptive status of her own body is effective. And so one must explain [it], for if he meant [it] there on account of a certain [claim], why did [the Mishnah] say that while she is still in her father's house, it is upon the father to bring proof that the blemishes developed after she was betrothed? Why must he bring proof if he says, "I am certain"? For it implies that in every case he must bring proof, even if the father says, "I am certain"! And to R"I, it seems [better] to explain here that they do not have a claim concerning virginity because she is in the presumptive status of a mukat etz [a woman whose hymen was torn accidentally]. And even though all [women] also suffer accidental injuries, nevertheless other women have a claim concerning virginity since they do not say that they are mukat etz; however, these — a deaf-mute and an imbecile — who cannot speak, are married in the presumptive status of being mukat etz. And so it appears [to be the case], for in most books they do not read above in the baraita anything other than: "A deaf-mute, an imbecile, and an ailonit have a fine," and nothing more, and "and they have a claim concerning virginity" is not written in most books. And according to R"I's explanation, [the Gemara] asks well: since [that baraita] says "they have a fine," evidently we do not consider them to have the presumptive status of mukat etz; whereas according to Rashi's explanation, what is [the Gemara] asking? Here too [in our baraita], we consider them to have the presumptive status of virgins, for we say now that she was violated after she was betrothed! And Rashba [of Sens] asked against R"I's explanation: why does [the Gemara] not answer [that] the one which teaches "they do not have a claim concerning virginity" is according to Rabbi Meir, who says in the first chapter (above, Ketubot 13a): "A mukat etz, whether he knew about her [condition] or did not know about her [condition], [receives] two hundred [zuz]," and the one which teaches "they have a claim concerning virginity" is according to the Rabbis, who say their ketubah is a maneh? And if you should say [it is] because [the baraita] teaches "a deaf-mute" similar to "an ailonit" — behold, perforce an ailonit herself does not lose her ketubah completely, for Rav Sheshet, who answers "this is Rabban Gamliel, and this is Rabbi Yehoshua," holds in the first chapter (11b): [if] he married her in the presumptive status of a virgin and she was found to be non-virgin, she has a ketubah of a maneh.
